importance_ranking.reason: Wooden cabins have extreme visual variation across sub-types — A-frame, log cabin, glamping pod, portable site office — and buyers (resort developers, homeowners, contractors) use the image to immediately identify whether the product matches their project aesthetic and structural intent. Wrong cabin type or finish visible in the image = immediate skip; no amount of text description substitutes for seeing the actual structure.

Cabin size, number of rooms, insulation type, and wood type are primary shortlisting criteria for project buyers — a resort developer specifying a 20x20 ft insulated pine cottage cannot substitute a 10x10 ft uninsulated plywood unit. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for project fit.

Price varies enormously with cabin size, wood species, insulation grade, and finish — a basic portable site cabin vs a fully insulated teak resort cottage can differ by an order of magnitude. Indian B2B buyers (resort developers, contractors) use the listed per-sq-ft rate as a primary budget-qualification signal before engaging; without a visible price anchor, shortlisting is impossible.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard portable fixed-size units (site offices, security cabins) are quoted per piece; custom prefab cottages and resort cabins are quoted per sq ft. Both units appear in the market — showing the unit is essential to prevent price misreading when comparing listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece is a real market ambiguity for wooden cabins; a buyer comparing a per-sq-ft resort cabin quote against a per-piece portable cabin quote without visible units will misread the price by a large factor. Unit must be shown alongside price.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in the Indian wooden cabin market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and no buyer searches by manufacturer brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: For high-value project purchases (resort cabins, custom cottages), buyers evaluate manufacturer capability, installation track record, and after-sales service during vendor selection — but this is a post-image/spec/price check, not a primary shortlisting signal. No brand commands recall-driven search in this category.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Floor area is the primary price driver for wooden cabins — a 10x10 ft portable unit vs a 30x20 ft resort cottage represents a non-interchangeable product class with a large price delta; buyers cannot substitute one size for another in a project context.

PUF vs Rockwool vs No Insulation defines the thermal performance tier and drives significant price and suitability differences — a resort cabin in a hill station requires PUF or Rockwool insulation while a site office may need none, making these non-interchangeable across buyer segments.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The exterior cladding material (solid timber planks, WPC boards, plywood, sandwich panel) is a primary durability and cost differentiator that buyers use to shortlist — a WPC-clad cabin and a solid pine-clad cabin have different weathering performance, maintenance requirements, and price points that are not captured by Wood Type or Structure Type alone.

While Cabin Size captures named dimensions (e.g., 20x20 ft), a standalone floor area spec in sq ft enables direct price-per-sq-ft comparison and project budgeting — buyers quoting per sq ft need this as a numeric field to calculate total project cost.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Wood species determines structural grade, durability, cost, and aesthetic — a seller receiving an RFQ specifying Teak Wood vs Pine Wood immediately knows whether they can supply the product and at what price tier, making this the most routing-critical spec.

Protection features (Termite Proof, Fire Retardant, Waterproof) define the treatment and construction standard required — sellers need this to confirm whether their standard product meets the buyer's compliance or environmental requirement before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot determine whether they can supply the product or provide an accurate price without knowing the required floor area — size is the primary cost driver for custom prefab wooden cabins and the first question any seller will ask.

A seller needs to know whether the cabin is for a resort/hospitality project, residential use, or a site office to determine the appropriate structural standard, insulation requirement, and finish — these are fundamentally different products with different supply chains.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: Wooden cabins are custom-fabricated structures where buyers frequently have a specific design reference — a resort developer may have an architect's rendering, a homeowner may have a reference photo of a cabin style they want replicated, or a buyer may have an existing cabin they want to match or extend. An uploaded image allows sellers to immediately assess design feasibility, structural complexity, and material requirements before responding, significantly improving quote accuracy for this high-value custom product.
